title: Unit – 2 : Session – 3 | Activities and Response of the Self
sections: Q1. The transaction between Self and Body is ONLY in the form of INFORMATION — the two forms are SENSATION (signals from Body to Self: sound, touch, taste, pain) and INSTRUCTION (signals from Self to Body: decisions to act, walk, eat). The Self never physically 'becomes' the body nor vice versa; the body sends sensations, the Self reads them by choice and instructs the body accordingly.

Q2. Self as SEER: the one who sees/understands — e.g., seeing a flower, it is 'I' who comprehend its colour and meaning, not the eye (eye is an instrument). DOER: the one who decides and does — e.g., 'I' decide to pick up the book; the hand merely executes. ENJOYER: the one who experiences the result — e.g., the sweetness is sensed by the tongue, but 'I' am the one who enjoys it. Thus the Self sees, decides and experiences; the body only senses and acts as instrument.

Q3. PROGRAM of the Self: (1) KNOWING — understanding the harmony in existence; (2) ASSUMING on that basis; (3) RECOGNISING relationships rightly; (4) FULFILLING them in behaviour and work — i.e., living with continuous happiness by ensuring right understanding, right feeling, and physical facility. Production, protection and right utilisation of physical facility concern only ONE of the four levels (the body's need) and are themselves only a sub-part of the program — hence they constitute LESS THAN ONE-FOURTH; the larger three-fourths is understanding, feeling and relationship.

Q4. In extreme pain, the sensation arrives, but the Self READS it by choice: reaction = panic, blame, despair, anger at others; response = acknowledging the pain, seeking cause and remedy calmly, even comforting others. MY INSTANCE: during a severe sports injury before an exam, my first reaction was anger and self-pity; on pausing and reading the sensation by choice, I responded by getting treatment, resting, and planning study around recovery. I learned that response keeps me self-organised while reaction hands my state over to circumstances.
